 Kate Middleton Celebrates Indian Fashion at the Earthshot Awards 2026 
 The Princess of Wales embraced the sustainability dress code.
 By Emily Burack Published: Nov 17, 2026 9:35 AM EST Save Article Share Article Chris Jackson // Getty Images 2 min read Kate Middleton has arrived at the Earthshot Prize Awards in Mumbai! The Princess of Wales looked stylish in a red and green anarkali by Mahima Mahajan. She accessorized with Queen Elizabeth’s Emerald Tassel Suite , a diamond and emerald necklace and matching earrings.
 Chris Jackson // Getty Images Kate on the green carpet. The dress, made from handwoven silk Georgette with traditional Banarasi gold detailing, features hand embroidery and glass bead embellishments. The fabric is a rich vermilion color, a shade created using vegetable-based dyes. Prince William, meanwhile, is wearing a bespoke bandhgala by Manish Malhotra.
 Chris Jackson // Getty Images The Waleses on the carpet. Other attendees to walk the green carpet included Simone Ashley , Rami Malek, and Alia Bhatt.
 Tonight is Kate’s third time attending Earthshot in the last six years. In 2021, she rewore an Alexander McQueen dress and in 2022, she rented an off-the-shoulder Solace London dress from the fashion rental platform HURR . At the first Earthshot awards, “guests were expected to wear, or re-wear, outfits with sustainability in mind,” and that dress code has seemingly stuck in the years following.
 Samir Hussein // Getty Images Kate at Earthshot 2021. Karwai Tang // Getty Images Kate at Earthshot 2022. Upon their arrival in India yesterday, the Waleses rode the Mumbai Metro and played a game of cricket. As she met well-wishers, Kate declined to sign an autograph, following royal protocol .
 Her style in Mumbai has already leaned into the theme of sustainability: Yesterday, the Princess of Wales rewore a royal blue Roksanda dress she debuted at Wimbledon while carrying a custom DeMellier bag from SurpRice rice straw. Earlier today, she rewore a linen Gabriela Hearst suit (also previously worn to Wimbledon ) and carried a custom Dior bag made with traditional Indian craftsmanship.
 Emily Burack Deputy Digital Editor Emily Burack (she/her) is the Deputy Digital Editor for Town & Country, where she covers entertainment, celebrities, the royals, and a wide range of other topics.
